lucas (docs): FYI I'm opening a tiny PR to fix a broken saved-panel link and add a short Ruby SDK header fallback example. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1501

maya (analytics): Thanks. The panel moved during the export -> import. New panel id is grafana:usage_tiering_alt_2026. Add a migration note + the panel id so customers can search/replace. Also mention the 'tier_bucket' label we use in metering.

frank (infra): Confirmed: Hosted panels keep old ids; export/import to new grafana namespaces changes ids. Docs should suggest steps to update bookmarks and saved alerts. Short how-to would be helpful.

olga (sdk): I'll add a tiny Ruby example to show reading headers with fallback. Keep it one method.

lucas (docs): Draft migration blurb: "If a saved panel 404s after the Grafana migration, search for grafana:usage_tiering_alt_2026 and replace the legacy panel id. For many dashboards, analytics can run a bulk fix; open an analytics ticket with dashboard ids attached." Thoughts?

maya (analytics): Perfect. Also add a note that 'tier_bucket' is the canonical label used in the CSV export and in alerts. If customers rebind alerts, they should map on that label.

olga (sdk): Ruby snippet (net/http):

```ruby
# prefer new header, fallback to legacy
def read_limit(resp)
  resp['X-RW-Rate'] || resp['X-Rate-Limit']
end

# usage: puts "limit=#{read_limit(response)}"
```

frank (infra): Can we add a short curl example showing both headers for ops teams? e.g., `curl -I` output sample. Keeps troubleshooting easier.

lucas (docs): Good idea. I'll include one-line curl sample and a compact compatibility table: legacy panel id -> grafana:usage_tiering_alt_2026, legacy headers -> X-RW-Rate/X-RW-Burst, affected: Hosted vs Dedicated. Keep it small.
